title: How does a line learn?
hook: No formula, no maths homework: just a line that is told when it is wrong.

knows: that a straight line can separate two groups of points
doesNotKnow: how a separating line can be learned by small corrections
that the perceptron changes only when it gets a point wrong

misconception: A line is fitted by one calculation; it cannot improve in small steps.
objective: The learner can explain that a perceptron checks points one at a time, changes its line only on a mistake, and each nudge moves the line toward putting the missed point on the right side.

claims.text: Starting from zero weights and sweeping (1,1)+, (−1,0)−, (2,−1)+, (−1,−2)−, (0,2)+ in order, the perceptron nudges at (1,1) (weights 1,1, offset 1) and at (−1,0) (weights 2,1, offset 0); the second sweep has no mistakes: 2 nudges in all.
claims.source: checkOne() / untilClean() in Demo.tsx with the rule w ← w + label·(x, y, 1) when label·score ≤ 0. Node: nudge at (1,1) → [1,1,1]; nudge at (−1,0) → [2,1,0]; sweep 1 mistakes 2, sweep 2 mistakes 0.

claims.text: In this toy a zero score counts as a mistake, which is why the very first point is nudged when there is no line yet.
claims.source: Toy convention stated on the stage (locked caption) and in Demo.tsx; brief 33 in company/domains/briefs/ai.md.

claims.text: A perceptron changes its weights only when it misclassifies a point, by adding or subtracting that point.
claims.source: Rosenblatt 1958, 'The perceptron: a probabilistic model for information storage and organization in the brain', Psychological Review 65(6); the error-correction rule in modern form: Bishop 2006, Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning, §4.1.7.

claims.text: Each nudge moves the line toward putting the missed point on the right side: the missed point's score rises by |point|² + 1 (for a + point) or falls by as much (for a − point).
claims.source: After w ← w + l·(x, y, 1), the point's score changes by l·(x² + y² + 1). Bishop 2006 §4.1.7 (the update reduces that point's error).

recall.question: A perceptron's line already puts a point on the correct side. What does that point do to the line on the next sweep?
options: Nothing: only mistakes change the line
Pulls the line a little closer to it
Pushes the line a little further away
recall.why: The perceptron updates only when it gets a point wrong (or scores it exactly 0). Correct points leave the weights alone.
